$note: Moat's words. One status vocabulary and one glossary for the web UI (web/src/format.ts reads this file) and macOS (MoatKit labels; web/src/copy.test.ts checks that the Swift labels match). Plain language first: a term that needs a technical word keeps that word under Details. docs/design.md explains the rules.

protected-session.label: Tasks protected
protected-session.meaning: Tasks you start through Moat run inside a tested boundary that exists before they launch.

enforced.label: Protected
enforced.meaning: Your rules decide which connections can leave this device, for the kinds of traffic it supports.

monitoring.label: Watching only
monitoring.meaning: Moat records connections here but does not block them yet.

dns-only.label: Web filter only
dns-only.meaning: Moat only sees which websites this device looks up. It can't see apps or connections, or count data.

degraded.label: Partly protected
degraded.meaning: Something your rules need isn't working on this device. See why below.

recovery-required.label: Needs you at the device
recovery-required.meaning: This device couldn't confirm its setup after a restart or update. It keeps its last checked rules and needs you at the device; nothing is reset or guessed.

rollback-pending.label: Undo didn't finish
rollback-pending.meaning: Undoing a trial change didn't finish, so the trial rules are still in force. Fix it at the device.

isolated.label: Locked down
isolated.meaning: Emergency lockdown: only the recovery paths you chose are open.

unknown.label: Can't confirm
unknown.meaning: We can't confirm this device is protected right now: it hasn't reported recently.

macCoverage.$note: macOS CoverageLevel raw values map onto the shared labels above.

glossary.means: What may connect where. Every change to your rules gets a version number, shown under Details.
A computer, phone or TV that Moat watches or protects.

glossary.say: checked just now / checked 5 min ago
glossary.means: When the device last reported. Older than 10 minutes, Moat says it can't confirm.
One attempt by an app to reach a server.
An exact program, recognised by its file and its signature, never by its name alone. The file path and signer are under Details.
Something you start through Moat, such as a coding agent, that runs inside a boundary with its own rules.
Moat recorded the connection but did not check it against a rule.
Your home's ad or DNS blocker (Pi-hole or AdGuard Home). For phones and TVs it is the only view Moat has.
An emergency switch that blocks new connections until you turn it off.
Watch one app do one job for a while, so you can decide what to allow.
What an app tried to reach while you recorded it. Nothing is allowed until you tick it.
The places you allowed for one app after a review. It never changes; new activity starts a new review.
Places an app started reaching after you approved its list.
Ready-made rules for common work (coding, package installs). Nothing is turned on until you choose.
The Moat hub that keeps your rules and collects reports from your devices. Devices keep working without it.
The key only you hold. Changes that allow more need it.
A narrow key for this phone or browser that can only approve what your owner key allows it to.
A stretch of time where reports were lost, so activity then is incomplete.

jargon.$note: Words that may not appear in headings, labels, buttons, chips, banners or explanations outside a Details disclosure (web/src/copy.test.ts). Data a device reported (hostnames, app names, reasons) is exempt.
